uwp_capture_status: ok — UWP launched via uwp-app-runner (pid 20020, windowTitle 'Disabling Screen Capture C# sample'); golden frame captured. Note: UWP CoreWindow exposed only the root Pane to UI Automation, so per-scenario nav/actuation could not be driven on the original app; the golden is the scenario-1 rendered frame (nav list + description + media player).
notes: Structural + behavioral parity gate = 100/100 (3/3 pass). WinUI 3 build+launch OK (pid 26272). WinUI UIA trees are fully populated (45 elements/scenario) and match the UWP content exactly (description text, MediaPlayerElement, ScenarioControl ListBox with all 3 items). WinUI screenshots render blank white: this is a winapp PrintWindow capture limitation for WinUI 3 windows hosting a MediaPlayerElement (composition overlay), NOT an empty page — so pixel visual parity was not verifiable, but textual/structural parity is strong. Scenario 2 additionally sets WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE, for which a blank capture is the correct intended behavior.

features.name: Enabling screen capture
features.note: WinUI UIA matches UWP: 'Description:', 'Screen capture allowed', 'By default, screen capture is allowed', plus MediaPlayerElement. WinUI screenshot blank due to MediaPlayerElement composition-capture limitation (not an empty page).

features.name: Disabling screen capture
features.note: Applies SetWindowDisplayAffinity(WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) on nav-in and WDA_NONE on nav-out — faithful WinUI 3 equivalent of UWP IsScreenCaptureEnabled=false. Blank capture here is the correct intended behavior; UIA tree present.

features.name: Managing AppCapture
features.note: AllowAppCaptureCheckBox ToggleSwitch present (cov 1/1) and wired to AppCapture.SetAllowedAsync. Toggle produced no visible status change (AppCapture status only changes during active capture — hardware-gated); no positive UWP baseline for this control, so flagged for manual review, not treated as a dead control.
